'''Roosevelt:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Bill Weld]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Bill Weld]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | image2 = File:1987 Mark Roosevelt Massachusetts House of Representatives (cropped).png | image_size = 150x150px | nominee2 = [[Mark Roosevelt]] | party2 = Democratic Party (United States) | running_mate2 = [[Bob Massie (activist)|Bob Massie]] | popular_vote2 = 611,650 | percentage2 = 28.27% }} {{ElectionsMA}} The '''1994 Massachusetts gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 1994. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Bill Weld]] won re-election as [[governor of Massachusetts]] by the largest margin in state history, winning every county and all but six of the state's [[List of municipalities in Massachusetts|351 municipalities]]. As of 2024, this is the most recent election in which [[Boston]], [[Somerville, Massachusetts|Somerville]], [[Lawrence, Massachusetts|Lawrence]], [[Chelsea, Massachusetts|Chelsea]], [[Brookline, Massachusetts|Brookline]], [[Northampton, Massachusetts|Northampton]], [[Provincetown]], [[Monterey, Massachusetts|Monterey]], [[Great Barrington, Massachusetts|Great Barrington]], [[Ashfield, Massachusetts|Ashfield]], [[Williamstown, Massachusetts|Williamstown]], [[Williamsburg, Massachusetts|Williamsburg]], [[Shelburne, Massachusetts|Shelburne]], [[Sunderland, Massachusetts|Sunderland]], and [[Pelham, Massachusetts|Pelham]] voted for the Republican candidate for governor.{{Cite web |title=1994 Gubernatorial General Election Results - Massachusetts |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?year=1994&fips=25&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=uselectionatlas.org}} ==Republican primary== ===Governor=== ====Candidates==== *[[Bill Weld]], incumbent governor ===Lieutenant governor=== ====Candidates==== *[[Paul Cellucci]], incumbent lieutenant governor Incumbent governor Bill Weld and Lieutenant Governor Paul Cellucci were unopposed for renomination. ==Democratic primary== ===Governor=== ====Candidates==== *[[George A. Bachrach]], former state senator from [[Watertown, Massachusetts|Watertown]] *[[Michael J. Barrett]], state senator from [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]] *[[Mark Roosevelt]], state representative from [[Back Bay, Boston|the Back Bay]] and member of the [[Roosevelt family]] In 1987, Barrett succeeded Bachrach as the senator from the Middlesex and Suffolk District. The district was composed of Cambridge, Belmont, Watertown, and the Allston-Brighton neighborhood of Boston. ===== Declined ===== *[[Joseph P. Kennedy II]], U.S. representative (1987–1999) In 1993, a ''Boston Globe'' poll showed Kennedy within one percentage point of popular incumbent [[William Weld]] in a hypothetical gubernatorial match-up, prompting prominent state Democrats to try and recruit him for the race.{{cite web|url=http://www.thecrimson.com/article/1993/2/22/kennedy-wont-run-pcambridge-democratic-leaders/|title=Kennedy Won't Run |work= [[The Harvard Crimson]]| publisher= | first= Wendy M. | last= Seltzer| date= February 22, 1993| access-date= June 7, 2023}} Though no other Democrat was polling near Weld, Kennedy decided to forgo the race and remain in Congress. ====Results==== [[File:Massachusetts Democratic gubernatorial primary results by municipality, 1994.svg|thumb|Primary results by municipality]] {{Election box begin no change | title=Massachusetts Democratic gubernatorial primary, 1994}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Mark Roosevelt]] |votes = 215,061 |percentage = 47.91% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[George Bachrach]] |votes = 120,567 |percentage = 26.86% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Michael J. Roosevelt won only six municipalities statewide ([[Amherst, Massachusetts|Amherst]], [[Cambridge, Massachusetts|Cambridge]], [[Leverett, Massachusetts|Leverett]], [[Otis, Massachusetts|Otis]], [[Shutesbury, Massachusetts|Shutesbury]] and [[Wendell, Massachusetts|Wendell]]).
